exposure: Hepatitis E virus (HEV) infection (anti-HEV IgG, anti-HEV IgM, HEV RNA positivity)
cohort: 528 pregnant women in their third trimester, including those with and without hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg).
finding: Anti-HEV IgG prevalence was high and increased with maternal age, correlating with higher infant birth weights, while anti-HEV IgM positivity was linked to an increased risk of neonatal infections and coinfection with HBV posed potential adverse obstetric outcomes.
